newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC TO ADOPT EUROPEAN MANAGEMENT STYLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC TO ADOPT EUROPEAN MANAGEMENT STYLE.

text.p: Celtic have decided to break from British practice and adopt a European style of management following their sacking of manager Tommy Burns.
Their decision, announced at a press conference on Saturday, could open the way for the appointment of former England manager Bobby Robson, currently coach at Barcelona.
Club chief executive Fergus McCann said Burns would be replaced by a two-tier operation, a general manager and a coach.
"We have not approached anyone yet but we will be looking closely in the next two months to get the right type of people to take this club into the future," McCann said.
Robson, who was approached to take over at Celtic in 1994 while at Porto, is ranked as a likely target.
The Celtic chief said the move towards the continental approach had come after studying the operations of several clubs in Italy, France and Gemany.
Ironically, the idea of pushing Celtic towards the continental style of management came from the departed Burns, who went to both Juventus and Ajax last year to study their set-ups.
